newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at day's floor, July/Sept shines.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at day's floor, July/Sept shines.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Monday lower with nearbys at the session's floor. Traders said a large block of July/Sept trade towards the close helped inflate the volume.
Volume doubled to more than 4,519 lots at the close from the midday break, with July and September accounting for the bulk of the turnover.
"It could be a pre-arranged trade or people just moving the position around," said one trader, referring to the July/Sept deal.
The market gapped higher at the outset but soon headed south on Far East origin selling and chart-triggered sell-stops, traders said.
Support to the market came mostly from light jobber buying.
September finished $40 down at $1,735 a tonne, the day's low. Light sell-stops emerged at $1,755 on the way down.
Its high-point was $1,785. On the charts, a key support was seen at $1,695, the June 11 low.
July/Sept switches were traded at $20 and $25.
Coffee's downside bias reflected prospects of frost-free Brazil winter this season, a build in New York certified coffee stocks and the destocking of finished products especially in Europe.
Slower demand for coffee during northern hemipshere summer was forcing some large supermarkets to destock coffee.
"This helps take out roaster buying on the nearbys," said one trader. "Also, there are no immediate prospects of a frost in Brazil.".
The U.S. June green coffee stock data due after the close of New York trading on Tuesday were expected to show a fall or an increase of 100,000 bags.
LIFFE June certified stock numbers were also due at lunchtime in London on Tuesday.
Options business was brisk, with 1,008 lots changing hands. Sept $1,500 puts and Sept $2,100 and $2,300 calls were active.
In other news, rumours of contract wash-outs and renegotiations swept the Indonesian coffee market amid tight supply.
There was also some rollover of positions from July to September because the sellers were not able to fix prices for the July contracts. Indonesia is the world's largest robusta coffee producer.
